issue.description:
Sources/PdftractCodegen/Methods.swift, VerifyReceipt(_:receipt:): runs the CLI's verify-receipt subcommand without --json and checks the result by trimming stdout and comparing to the literal string true.

This is inconsistent with every other method in this SDK, which all pass --json and decode a typed model, and it discards whatever detail the CLI might report about why a receipt failed verification (which of several checks failed, expected vs actual hash, etc) -- the caller only ever learns true or false.

Fix: pass --json to the verify-receipt invocation (assuming the pdftract CLI supports it there, same as extract/hash/classify) and decode a small structured result type (e.g. valid: Bool, reason: String?) instead of doing a raw string comparison on trimmed stdout.

Source: Sources/PdftractCodegen/Methods.swift is marked GENERATED -- fix needs to land in the pdftract codegen template (jedarden/pdftract); note the cross-repo dependency when resolving.

issue.description:
Sources/PdftractCodegen/Methods.swift, both ExtractStream and Search: when a line from the CLI's NDJSON output fails JSON decoding, the catch block is empty except for a comment (// Skip malformed lines; the final error will be reported if needed / // Skip malformed lines) -- the line is dropped with zero signal to the caller.

Effect: a truncated write, a CLI bug emitting a malformed line, or a schema drift between the CLI and this SDK's Page/Match models all look identical to clean output that simply had fewer pages/matches than expected -- there's no way for a caller to distinguish silently-lost data from a PDF that genuinely had fewer results.

Fix: at minimum, surface a count of skipped/undecodable lines (e.g. via a side-channel callback, a final summary value, or by finishing the stream with a warning-carrying error type) instead of swallowing decode failures unconditionally.

Source: Sources/PdftractCodegen/Methods.swift is marked GENERATED -- fix needs to land in the pdftract codegen template (jedarden/pdftract); note the cross-repo dependency when resolving.
issue.title: Surface silently-dropped malformed JSON lines in ExtractStream/Search

issue.description:
Sources/PdftractCodegen/Types.swift, Source.bytes(let data) case in toArgs(): writes the PDF bytes to a new temp file under FileManager.default.temporaryDirectory (pdftract-input-UUID.pdf) so the CLI can read it, but nothing ever deletes that file afterward -- not in toArgs(), not in exec() after the process completes.

Effect: every call using Source.bytes(...) leaks one temp file per invocation, and for sensitive documents passed in-memory specifically to avoid touching disk, the PDF content ends up written to a shared temp directory anyway and stays there.

Fix: track the temp file path created in toArgs() and remove it after exec() (or the streaming equivalents) complete, including on the error path. Source: Sources/PdftractCodegen/Types.swift is marked GENERATED -- fix needs to land in the pdftract codegen template (jedarden/pdftract) to survive regeneration; note the cross-repo dependency when resolving.

issue.description:

Every generated public method in Sources/PdftractCodegen/Methods.swift is PascalCase (Extract, ExtractText, ExtractMarkdown, ExtractStream, Search, GetMetadata, Hash, Classify, VerifyReceipt). Sources/PdftractCodegen/Methods.swift, Pdftract.findBinary(): rescans the full PATH (FileManager.fileExists check only) on every Pdftract() init with no caching, and does not check the found file is actually executable (isExecutableFile(atPath:) would be more correct than fileExists(atPath:)).

issue.description:
README.md's Troubleshooting section states: The SDK will refuse to invoke mismatched binary versions. Install the correct version from the releases page.

There is no such check anywhere in the code. .codegen-version (currently 1.1.0) is never read at runtime by Sources/Pdftract or Sources/PdftractCodegen -- grep confirms no reference to codegen-version or any version-comparison logic in exec() or anywhere else. A user running an incompatible pdftract binary gets whatever error the mismatched CLI happens to produce, not a clear refuse-to-invoke message.

Either: (a) implement the check -- e.g. exec() runs pdftract --version once (cached) and compares against the SDK's own .codegen-version, throwing a clear PdftractError before attempting real work on mismatch, or (b) remove the claim from README.md if the check isn't going to be implemented soon, so the docs stop promising a safety net that doesn't exist.
issue.title: Implement or remove the binary version-compatibility check claimed in README

issue.description:
Sources/PdftractCodegen/Methods.swift's private exec() (used by every non-streaming method: Extract, ExtractText, ExtractMarkdown, GetMetadata, Hash, Classify, VerifyReceipt) calls process.run() then process.waitUntilExit() BEFORE reading from outPipe/errPipe (the reads happen after waitUntilExit() returns).

If the pdftract CLI writes more JSON to stdout than the OS pipe buffer holds (typically 64KB on Linux) -- plausible for a multi-page or image-heavy PDF's --json output -- the child process blocks on write() because nothing is draining the pipe, while the parent is blocked in waitUntilExit() waiting for the child to exit. Classic Process/Pipe deadlock; the call hangs forever (or until a caller-imposed timeout external to this code kills it).

Note this repo's own ExtractStream and Search methods already read the pipe concurrently with the process running (readData(ofLength:) in a while process.isRunning loop) and do not have this bug -- exec() should use the same pattern: drain stdout/stderr concurrently (e.g. via a Task reading while waiting, or Pipe's readabilityHandler) rather than reading only after waitUntilExit().

Source: Sources/PdftractCodegen/Methods.swift is marked GENERATED -- do not edit manually. This needs to be fixed in the pdftract codegen template (jedarden/pdftract) so it propagates on next regen; track that cross-repo dependency in this bead's resolution.
issue.title: Fix Process/Pipe deadlock risk in Methods.swift exec() for large PDF output

issue.description:
The README positions this as a server-side Swift SDK where every method is async throws, but nothing documents whether a single Pdftract instance may be shared across concurrent Tasks/actors (is it Sendable? is per-call state in exec() isolated?), nor whether the emitted models (Document, Page, Block, SearchMatch, Fingerprint, Classification, Metadata) are safely passed across concurrency domains. Distinct from pdfswift-b64f41eb (process cancellation/timeout) and pdfswift-6bc41168 (stderr drain), which cover process lifecycle, not client shareability. Work: audit the generated code for mutable per-instance state, add Sendable conformance where sound, and document the concurrency contract in the README. All touched paths (Sources/PdftractCodegen/*, Sources/Pdftract/Pdftract.swift, README.md) are generator output, so the change must land in jedarden/pdftract's templates/sdk-sweep/swift templates and be regenerated per docs/notes/codegen-refresh.md, with pdftract sdk validate run before commit.

issue.notes:
Verification run per acceptance criteria; criterion 2 (XCTSkip guard) VERIFIED GREEN, criterion 1 (green with real binary) FAILED - cannot be met, defect is in the generated client not the test.

Setup: clean extraction of HEAD 7dc0e749 at /tmp/pdfswift-verify-zKer (retained for diagnosis); docker swift:5.10-jammy; swift test --filter ExtractStreamConformanceTests. Binary: jedarden/pdftract Forgejo release v1.2.0 x86_64-unknown-linux-musl (sha256 f86d7274e89aa22d1faa13db8ab900344c4cd6fedc52e444094512f7d33152fa verified against release SHA256SUMS), mounted at /usr/local/bin/pdftract.

Run A (no binary on PATH): Executed 4 tests, 4 skipped, 0 failures, suite passed, exit 0. Skip fires at ExtractStreamConformanceTests.swift:68 as designed.

Run B (real v1.2.0 binary): Executed 4 tests, 5 failures (2 unexpected), exit 1:
- testStreamedPageBlocksMatchExtract threw PdftractCodegen.CorruptPdfError: the generated client sends 'extract --json <input>' but the v1.2.0 CLI defines --json <PATH> (output path, '-' for stdout), so clap rejects the argv with exit 2 ('required arguments were not provided: <INPUT>') and the SDK exit-code table mislabels that as CorruptPdfError.
- extractStream is equally broken: CLI --ndjson emits per-BLOCK records {page, block_index, kind, bbox, spans}; the client decodes each line as Page (needs page_index/width/height/rotation/blocks), every line fails decoding and is silently dropped (onSkippedLine nil by default), so extractStream yields 0 pages and finishes cleanly. Evidence: testPagesArriveInDocumentOrder failed 0 != 4; testPageIndexIsZeroBasedAndIncrementing failed 0 != 3.
- Even with corrected argv ('extract --json - <input>' - verified against the binary: 3 pages, exit 0), the JSON still cannot decode into the SDK's Document/Page: CLI page keys are {blocks, index, spans, tables} (no page_index, no width/height/rotation) while the generated Page requires page_index/width/height/rotation/spans/blocks.
- testTrivialEmptyPdfYieldsZeroPages exposed an additional binary-side break: v1.2.0 exits 1 ('Document contains no pages') for a structurally valid zero-page PDF, where README/test expect an empty stream, not an error.

Root cause is in jedarden/pdftract, not this repo: templates/sdk-skeleton/swift/Sources/PdftractCodegen/Methods.swift.tera (codegen-version 1.2.0) models a CLI that does not exist - CLI --ndjson emits block records while pdftract-core's page-frame protocol (crates/pdftract-core/src/output/ndjson/frames.rs, header/page/footer) is wired only to the Python bindings, never to the CLI. The test is correct: it failed against a real binary because the documented parity contract is genuinely broken in the generated client.

No file changes made here: the fix belongs in the pdftract Tera templates plus regeneration (editing generated code in this repo would be overwritten by the next codegen). Filed proposal for the protocol fix. Not closing: acceptance criterion 1 unmet.

Scope: Tests/PdftractTests/ExtractStreamConformanceTests.swift tests testPagesArriveInDocumentOrder and testPageIndexIsZeroBasedAndIncrementing — the documented contract that streamed pages arrive in document order and page.pageIndex is zero-based and incrementing per the README convention. The suite is committed on origin/main (78910f76) but no green run against a real pdftract binary has been recorded (prior attempts hit max_turns before verification).

Acceptance criteria:
- Both tests pass in the cached docker swift:5.10-jammy harness (filtered suite — bare `swift test` fails on ConformanceTests) with a real pdftract binary available.
- Both throw XCTSkip (not fail) when no binary is on PATH.
- Run output recorded as verification evidence on this bead.
issue.notes:
VERIFICATION COMPLETED — acceptance criteria 1 CANNOT pass: the two tests fail against the only real binary (pdftract v1.2.0, x86_64-musl release, SHA256SUMS-verified tarball f86d7274e89aa22d). Criterion 2 PASSES: with no binary on PATH all 4 tests in the class XCTSkip cleanly, suite green.

RUN A (real binary on PATH, clean HEAD extraction): swift test --filter ExtractStreamConformanceTests in docker swift:5.10-jammy -> Executed 4 tests, with 5 failures (2 unexpected), exit 1. testPagesArriveInDocumentOrder: pages.count 0 != 4; testPageIndexIsZeroBasedAndIncrementing: 0 != 3 and [] != [0,1,2]; testStreamedPageBlocksMatchExtract threw CorruptPdfError; testTrivialEmptyPdfYieldsZeroPages threw PdftractError.

ROOT CAUSE (verified by driving pdftract v1.2.0 directly on an identical synthesized fixture, bypassing the SDK): generated SDK templates are drifted from the real binary contract on three points.
(1) extract --ndjson emits BLOCK-level records {page, block_index, kind, bbox, spans} — no page_index, no width/height/rotation, no blocks array, and NO TEXT (spans empty). The client (Methods.swift extractStream) JSON-decodes each line as Page (requires page_index/width/height/rotation/spans/blocks), every line fails decode and is silently dropped (onSkippedLine default nil) -> stream of 0 pages, no error. Even a corrected decoder could not satisfy the order test: the marker text is absent from NDJSON output entirely.
(2) buffered extract() builds ['extract','--json',<input-path>] but the binary's --json takes a PATH value (use '-' for stdout): the input path is consumed as the output path, leaving no input -> clap usage error exit 2 -> mapError(2) -> CorruptPdfError. Same flag-shape defect in extractText/extractMarkdown (--text/--md consume the following --json token as their value).
(3) zero-page PDF: binary exits 1 'Document contains no pages', so testTrivialEmptyPdfYieldsZeroPages' clean-empty-stream expectation contradicts binary behavior.
pdftract source (~/pdftract) contains block_index but page_index appears NOWHERE in src — Types.swift's page_index coding key matches no binary output. No page-level streaming flag exists in v1.2.0 (--format ndjson requires -o file output; --ndjson is the only stdout stream mode).

NOT FIXED HERE by intent: Types.swift/Methods.swift are GENERATED from Tera templates in jedarden/pdftract — hand edits die at next regen; a faithful fix needs template redesign (client-side block->page grouping or a binary page-level NDJSON mode incl. text) plus possibly a binary change for the zero-page contract. Filed cross-repo proposal on the pdftract workspace; do not retry this bead as-is — it stays red until that proposal lands. issue.description:
The README documents the `.url(URL(...))` source and lists `SourceUnreachableError` (4), `RemoteFetchInterruptedError` (5), and `TlsError` (6), but nothing documents the actual fetch behavior those errors wrap: connect/read timeout values, whether redirects are followed (and how many hops), TLS verification strictness, proxy handling, and any response-size or content-type limits. Existing test beads (pdfswift-c84b293b, pdfswift-a53be3d4) cover that exit codes map to error types and that the APIs run — not the fetch semantics. Close the gap by capturing the pdftract CLI's URL-fetch behavior (verify against the real binary per pdfswift-3307a377), documenting it in the README near the `.url` example, and adding tests that pin the observable semantics (e.g., an unreachable host yields SourceUnreachableError, a bad certificate yields TlsError, an interrupted transfer yields RemoteFetchInterruptedError).

issue.description:
Split child 1 of umbrella pdfswift-6bc41168. Land the reworked regression-test watchdog currently sitting UNCOMMITTED in Tests/PdftractTests/ConformanceTests.swift.

Why the committed watchdog is insufficient: fef69c4 joins the consumer in a task group and calls cancelAll() on timeout. That cannot recover a real stderr backpressure deadlock — the consumer is blocked inside readData(ofLength:), cancelling it fires the stream's onTermination, and onTermination's process.terminate() + waitUntilExit() blocks too because the child is stuck in write() on a full stderr pipe. cancelAll() wedges and the suite hangs anyway.

The working tree already contains the replacement: the consumer runs detached, hands its DrainOutcome back through a DrainBox actor, the test polls the box instead of awaiting the consumer, and on timeout SIGKILLs the fake child via a pidfile the fake writes at startup (SIGKILL not SIGTERM — dash defers SIGTERM while blocked in write(); killing the shell, the only holder of the stdout write end, EOFs the deadlocked read and unwedges the run).

Scope: Tests/PdftractTests/ConformanceTests.swift ONLY. No production code changes.

Acceptance criteria:
- All four StreamingStderrRegressionTests cases route through the hardened drain(_:killChild:) harness.
- The timeout path SIGKILLs the fake child through its pidfile and fails an assertion instead of hanging the suite.
- The commit touches only Tests/PdftractTests/ConformanceTests.swift, is committed on main, and pushed to Forgejo origin (never github directly).
issue.notes: Re-verified on re-dispatch (prior run had landed everything but left the bead open): fresh git fetch confirms origin/main == main == 40b7077 on Forgejo with zero unpushed commits; commit touches only Tests/PdftractTests/ConformanceTests.swift (+120/-32); all four StreamingStderrRegressionTests call sites (lines 346/365/384/414) route through drain(_:killChild:) with no task-group harness remnants (withTaskGroup/cancelAll/group.next survive only in the doc comment explaining why they were replaced); timeout path confirmed as fake writes 'echo $$ > pid' at startup, watchdog polls DrainBox at 50ms ticks, and on budget exhaustion killFakeChild -> kill(pid, SIGKILL) then DrainOutcome(finished: false), which fails the finished assertion. Working tree has no uncommitted change to the test file, so no new commit was needed.

codegen-refresh.md covers producing, validating, and committing a refreshed drop (step 5: commit the drop plus the `.codegen-version` bump), but there is no documented checklist for cutting an actual SDK release — which `--version` to stamp so README/Package.swift agree, tagging semver on origin, and confirming the tag actually reached the GitHub mirror that SwiftPM's `from:` requirement resolves against. The v1.1.0 tag work (bf-4mw, resolved per plan.md) was done ad hoc; write the repeatable checklist into docs/notes, including verifying the tag is visible on the mirror via `git ls-remote` before announcing the release.

---
Priority: P3
Created by: weave strand

VERDICT: the ranged-GET read deadline is ~10 s TOTAL-TIME-based (not idle-gap), but firing it never stops the process — the identical ranged GET is re-issued indefinitely, so any GET whose body takes longer than ~10 s total (stalled OR legitimately slow) hangs pdftract extract with empty stderr until externally killed. There is NO effective process-level read/stall timeout; observed minimum hang = the 90 s probe cap (exit 124, 8 identical GET attempts logged server-side, no backoff/escalation).

1. Probe 1 http://127.0.0.1:18765/slow/body/15000 (15 s mid-body stall; HEAD answered instantly): wall 90004 ms, exit 124 (external 90 s cap), stderr EMPTY. Server log: HEAD + 8 identical ranged GETs (Range: bytes=0-65535) at +10.13/+10.24 s spacing until kill.
2. Continuous 100 ms data flow still cut at 10.0 s per attempt ⇒ TOTAL-TIME semantics, NOT idle-gap (an idle/read timeout would have completed at ~20 s).

Cut by the client's own ~10 s deadline (not the 90 s cap, not the 120 s server cap); exactly one HEAD, no retry. Observed minimum no-response hang: 10.2 s.
4. Probe 4 (TLS row, standing ruling verbatim): TLS unusable with self-signed; timeout not observable. Fresh corroboration: https://127.0.0.1:18443/slow/body/15000 → 7 ms, exit 1, 'HEAD request failed: connection interrupted' (https /ok.pdf identical: 8 ms). issue.description:
Child 3 of 4 (umbrella pdfswift-8281c238). Measures the read/stall (mid-transfer) timeout. Depends on pdfswift-de5ba934 (connect-phase results + same binary/harness from pdfswift-1d763709).

ANTI-MAX-TURNS RULES (this parent failed 3x by burning turns on hung probes):
- NEVER run a probe without an external cap: `timeout 90 <bin> extract <url>`.
- Run probes in background and poll, or batch in one script run; no foreground wait longer than ~2 min per tool call.

Probes (each capturing wall-clock ms via date +%s%3N, exit code, verbatim stderr):
1. HTTP  http://127.0.0.1:18765/slow/body/15000  (headers + first byte sent, body stalls 15 s)
2. HTTP  http://127.0.0.1:18765/trickle/20       (body trickles at 20 ms/byte-class — tests idle-gap vs total-time semantics)
3. HTTP  http://127.0.0.1:18765/hang            (accepts request, never responds — server caps at 120 s)
4. TLS   https://127.0.0.1:18443/slow/body/15000
If a prior probe left the answer unambiguous for a route (e.g. slow/body resolved during child 2's batch), cite that run instead of rerunning — do not repeat checks with unchanged inputs.
Record whether plain HTTP and HTTPS differ, and whether the timeout is idle-based or total-time-based (trickle vs slow/body comparison gives this).

Acceptance criteria:
1. For each probe: recorded wall-clock duration, exit code, stderr text, cited verbatim.
2. A stated read/stall timeout value per scheme, OR the explicit no-timeout finding with the observed minimum hang duration.
3. An explicit statement (with evidence) of idle-gap vs total-time semantics, or 'undetermined' with why.
4. No Swift source or README changes. Preserve unrelated working-tree changes. Evidence on this bead's notes; the doc write is child 4's job.
issue.notes:
STANDING RULING for probe 4 (TLS row) — handed off from parent pdfswift-a197a9c8, consolidated by pdfswift-bd6ac6b4 (2026-09-29): the probe-4 TLS row (https://127.0.0.1:18443/slow/body/15000) must record exactly 'TLS unusable with self-signed; timeout not observable' instead of a timeout value — no timeout number, estimate, or placeholder. Reason: the v1.2.0 remote cli trusts only its compiled-in webpki-roots (ureq 2.12.1/rustls 0.23.40; rustls-native-certs, native-tls, openssl absent from the lockfile), so SSL_CERT_FILE/SSL_CERT_DIR are inert — every variant exits 1 'HEAD request failed: connection interrupted' during the handshake, while the 18443 listener itself is healthy (s_client completes with Verify return code 18). The connect phase itself never succeeds over TLS with this binary, so the read-stall phase over TLS is unreachable, not merely unmeasured. Binary to use (unchanged): ~/scratch/pdfswift-1d763709/probe-tmp/bin/pdftract-remote, --version 'pdftract 0.1.0', sha256 07f95264e59395a30ae622e42c7bd5f882583a20091a89c3ba665c9f16c48e0d. Evidence: ~/scratch/pdfswift-1d763709/tls-trust/ (transcript.md, b5-* listener proof, a7-* recipe matrix). Fix if ever needed (source change, then re-pin binary identity): ureq 'native-certs' feature, or AgentBuilder::tls_config + a --ca-file flag. When you record your probe results in these notes (notes replace wholesale), carry that exact sentence verbatim into the probe-4 row. Your HTTP probes 1-3 are unaffected and proceed normally.

=== READ-PHASE RESULTS (claude-code-glm-5.3-flash, 2026-09-29T23:4xZ) ===

Setup: binary identity re-verified before use — sha256 07f95264e59395a30ae622e42c7bd5f882583a20091a89c3ba665c9f16c48e0d, --version 'pdftract 0.1.0'. Same harness as child 2 (server.py at ~/pdftract-swift/docs/notes/probes/, still listening on 127.0.0.1:18765 HTTP + 127.0.0.1:18443 TLS, logging /tmp/probe-http.jsonl). /slow/body/<MS> = response headers + first body byte sent immediately, then MS ms of mid-body silence, then the rest; HEAD is answered instantly (headers only), so any stall below happens inside the ranged-GET body read — a clean read-phase probe for this HEAD-first client. Every probe: timeout 90 pdftract-remote extract <url>, wall-clock via date +%s%3N, stderr captured verbatim, all probes batched in one background script run (~/scratch/pdfswift-1d763709/probe-tmp/read-phase-probes.sh). Raw output: read-probes.txt; per-probe stderr: read-stderr/*.err.

VERDICT — the ranged-GET read deadline is ~10 s TOTAL-TIME-based, but firing it does NOT stop the process: the identical GET is re-issued indefinitely, so a mid-body stall (or any GET slower than ~10 s) hangs the CLI with no error, no stderr, until externally killed. There is NO effective process-level read/stall timeout.

1. Probe 1 — http://127.0.0.1:18765/slow/body/15000 (15 s mid-body stall): wall 90004 ms, exit 124 (killed by the external 90 s timeout cap, NOT by the client). stderr (verbatim): EMPTY — no error was ever surfaced. Server log: HEAD answered instantly at t=...076.893, then the IDENTICAL ranged GET (Range: bytes=0-65535) re-issued 8 times at +10.13/+10.24 s spacing until the kill — a forever retry loop, ~10.2 s per attempt.

2. Probe 2 — /trickle/20 as specified is NOT runnable against this client: wall 7 ms, exit 1, stderr (verbatim):
Error: Failed to download remote PDF

Caused by:
    Server does not support Range requests
   Reason: /trickle/<S> answers 200 with no Accept-Ranges (server.py: only /ok.pdf, /slow/connect, /slow/body, /slow/rangestall, /rangetrickle are 206-capable); the client refuses instantly — no timeout measurable on that route. Ran its purpose-built 206-capable twin instead: http://127.0.0.1:18765/rangetrickle/20 (headers instantly, then 1 byte per 100 ms for 20 s total — inter-byte gaps 100 ms, far below any plausible idle threshold; total 20 s, above the ~10 s deadline). Result: wall 90003 ms, exit 124 (external cap), stderr EMPTY, server log shows the identical ranged GET re-issued 8 times at +10.00/+10.01 s spacing. A continuously-trickling body was still cut at 10.0 s per attempt ⇒ the deadline is TOTAL-TIME from request start, NOT idle-gap based. An idle-gap read timeout would have let this transfer complete at ~20 s.

3. Probe 3 — http://127.0.0.1:18765/hang (request accepted, never answered): wall 10243 ms, exit 1, stderr (verbatim):
Error: Failed to open remote PDF source

Caused by:
    HEAD request failed: request timeout
   Cut by the client's own ~10 s deadline (not the 90 s cap, not the 120 s server cap). Observed minimum hang duration for the no-response case: 10.2 s. Server log: exactly one HEAD, no repeats — the HEAD-phase timeout surfaces cleanly as an error, unlike the body phase.

4. Probe 4 (TLS row, per standing ruling): TLS unusable with self-signed; timeout not observable. Fresh corroboration this attempt: https://127.0.0.1:18443/slow/body/15000 → wall 7 ms, exit 1, stderr (verbatim):
Error: Failed to open remote PDF source

Caused by:
    HEAD request failed: connection interrupted
   (https happy path identical: 8 ms, exit 1, same message.) The read-stall phase over TLS is unreachable because the handshake fails first.

5. Sub-deadline control — http://127.0.0.1:18765/slow/body/5000 (5 s mid-body stall): wall 5016 ms, exit 0, stderr empty, exactly one ranged GET, no retries. Brackets the deadline from below: stalls under ~10 s total succeed cleanly; ~10 s or above never complete. Consistent with child 2's 8 s TTFB control (exit 0) on the same deadline family. Baseline /ok.pdf: 55 ms, exit 0.

6. HTTP vs HTTPS: not comparable on this harness — plain HTTP shows the ~10 s per-attempt deadline and the unbounded retry hang; HTTPS never gets past the handshake (ruling above).

MECHANISM (source-corroborated, v1.2.0 tree ~/scratch/pdfswift-1d763709/probe-tmp/pdftract-v120-src): crates/pdftract-core/src/source/http_range.rs:26 const CONNECT_TIMEOUT_SECS: u64 = 10 (misnamed — it is the overall request deadline, not connect-only), applied at :132 as ureq AgentBuilder::timeout on the agent used for BOTH the HEAD and every ranged GET; ureq 2.12.1's agent-wide timeout runs from request start through body read ⇒ total-time semantics. fetch_range (:297) maps a body-read failure to io::ErrorKind::Interrupted ('Failed to read response body'); read_range/read/prefetch contain no retry loop, so the endless identical GETs are the upstream std Interrupted-retry idiom (Read::read_exact et al. ignore ErrorKind::Interrupted and re-issue) colliding with a per-request deadline. The retry has no observed bound, no backoff, no escalation, and swallows the error entirely (empty stderr at kill). The separate READ_TIMEOUT_SECS=30 (:29) is the NON-range fallback full-download path (download_to_temp_and_mmap_with_hook :722), not the ranged path.

DEFECT STATEMENT for child 4's doc (umbrella pdfswift-8281c238): any origin response whose ranged-GET body takes longer than ~10 s total — a stalled server OR a legitimately slow/large transfer — hangs pdftract extract indefinitely (retry loop, empty stderr, unbounded; killed externally at the 90 s probe cap after 8 identical attempts). The HEAD/TTFB phase by contrast errors out cleanly at ~10 s ('HEAD request failed: request timeout'), and the connect phase at ~30 s (child 2: blackhole 30035 ms). Suggested fix shape (for a future bead, not this one): map body-read timeout to a non-Interrupted error kind (or add a bounded retry with escalation) and consider separating a true idle/read timeout from the overall request deadline.

Constraints honored: no Swift source or README changes; measurement-only, no commits made; unrelated working-tree changes (.beads checkpoint files, .needle-predispatch-sha) untouched. Durable doc write remains child 4's job per bead description.

issue.description:
codegen-refresh.md warns that omitting --version stamps 0.1.0 into .codegen-version, the README install snippet, and the release link — but the only safeguard is prose. sdk validate deliberately ignores .codegen-version (per the doc), and the CI regenerate-and-diff (pdfswift-5efd262c) cannot catch a wrong stamp if it regenerates with the same wrong version. Add a cheap gate check (script or unit test) asserting one version literal appears consistently in .codegen-version, README's `from:` requirement, and README's release link, failing the gate loudly on mismatch.

issue.description:
No documented API bounds how long the subprocess may run or defines what happens when a consumer cancels the Task wrapping an in-flight extract/search or drops an extractStream sequence early. Cancellation must propagate to Process termination (kill + reap the child), an optional timeout should be available on exec(), and tests must prove a cancelled/dropped call does not leave an orphaned pdftract process or a caller blocked on a full Pipe. Document the resulting semantics in the README. Distinct from bf-um4 (which covers the stdout/stderr drain deadlock, not lifecycle).

Created by: weave strand

issue.description:
PROPOSAL (generated discovery from verification of pdfswift-23785038 - needs explicit admission, do not self-approve).

The generated Swift client (Sources/PdftractCodegen, codegen-version 1.2.0) cannot drive any released pdftract binary: all binary-facing methods are non-functional. Demonstrated against pdftract v1.2.0 (musl, sha256 f86d7274) with the real-binary conformance run recorded on pdfswift-23785038:

1. extract/extractText/extractMarkdown argv: client sends 'extract --json <input>' / '<input> --text --json'; the CLI defines --json/--md/--text as value-taking output paths ('-' = stdout). Every call dies as a clap usage error (exit 2), which the SDK exit table mislabels CorruptPdfError. Correct stdout shape is 'extract --json - <input>' (verified working).
2. JSON schema: CLI page object is {blocks, index, spans, tables}, blocks {bbox, kind, spans, text}; generated Page requires page_index/width/height/rotation/spans/blocks. Document decoding fails even after the argv fix.
3. extractStream: CLI --ndjson emits per-block records {page, block_index, kind, bbox, spans}; the client decodes lines as Page, so every line is silently dropped and the stream yields 0 pages. Parity between extract() and extractStream() (README contract, ExtractStreamConformanceTests) is untestable until this is fixed.
4. Zero-page PDFs: CLI exits 1 'Document contains no pages' for a structurally valid 0-page PDF; README/test expect an empty stream.

Fix belongs in jedarden/pdftract templates/sdk-skeleton/swift/*.tera (Methods.swift.tera argv + Types.swift.tera schema) AND a CLI-side page-level NDJSON wire format - pdftract-core already has the header/page/footer frame protocol (crates/pdftract-core/src/output/ndjson/frames.rs + pipeline.rs) but it is wired only to the Python bindings, never to the CLI. Decide the canonical wire protocol, wire it into the CLI (or realign the templates to block records), fix zero-page handling, regenerate pdftract-swift via 'pdftract sdk codegen', validate with 'pdftract sdk validate', then re-run the ExtractStreamConformanceTests verification on pdfswift-23785038 against a real binary - that bead stays open until this lands.

issue.description:
The README's error-handling section documents the exit-code-to-error-type table and the two SDK lifecycle errors, but says nothing about where the pdftract binary's stderr output goes when a command fails. The SDK reads the child's stderr (the streaming-stderr drain work in pdfswift-6bc41168/bf-um4 depends on reading it), yet no bead covers what the caller actually sees: whether captured stderr is attached to the thrown PdftractError's message, logged, or discarded. This is distinct from bf-338 (surfacing silently-dropped malformed NDJSON lines in stream payloads) — this is about the CLI's human-readable diagnostics on failure. Close the gap by: (1) deciding and implementing the surfacing mechanism (e.g., append truncated stderr to PdftractError's localizedDescription or expose a stderr field on the error), and (2) documenting the behavior in the README's error-handling section, plus a regression test asserting stderr text is (or is deliberately not) reachable from a caught error.

issue.description:
The README presents extractStream as the primary path for large PDFs, yielding per-page results (page.pageIndex, page.blocks), but no bead covers its functional output. The stream-related beads only target stderr draining (pdfswift-9d5bbcc5, pdfswift-6bc41168) and malformed-line surfacing (bf-338), and the coverage-completion bead pdfswift-a53be3d4 enumerates extractText, extractMarkdown, hash, classify, and .url/.bytes sources but omits extractStream (search is separately covered by pdfswift-41c46c80). Add conformance tests asserting: pages arrive in document order, pageIndex increments from 0 per the documented convention, the per-page blocks match what extract() returns for the same input, and a trivial/empty PDF yields zero pages. Gate them behind the XCTSkip guards from pdfswift-8f868708 since they need a real binary, and update pdfswift-a53be3d4's enumeration so the gap is tracked as closed.
